title: The Oath of Highmoor
premise: Bram Halloran, a temple scribe indentured to the corrupt Highmoor Concord, is ordered to interrogate a feral child who speaks the dead language of Thornfell, a kingdom erased from every map and record two centuries ago. The child, Wren, carries a living ember of the last dragon-fire, and the Concord's High Prior means to burn the country's hidden door open and seize the dragon's hoard of concentrated power. Bram, whose smuggler's knowledge of the mountains is the only map that still exists, flees with Wren into the Thornfells, gathering a found family of outcasts — a disgraced knight, a heretic archivist, and a smuggler queen — while the Concord hunts them and the ember gutters toward darkness. At the door of vanished Thornfell, Bram must choose between restoring a dead kingdom's power to the world or letting it die; he lets it die, breaking the Concord's claim to inherited power, and the survivors build something new that belongs to no crown or creed.
about_author: Rosalind Ravensworth spent a decade cataloguing marginalia in mountain monasteries before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the dust and ink of that life. She writes fantasy about people the histories forgot, from a stone cottage she refuses to locate on any map.

chapters.title: Ink and Indenture
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. We meet Bram copying ledgers in the Highmoor temple, his debt to the Concord tallied to the copper, his nights guiding smugglers through Thornfell passes for coin. He is competent, cynical, and quietly desperate. Emotional beat: the suffocating weight of belonging to something that owns you.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A mud-caked child appears at the temple's postern gate during a storm, speaking a language no scribe recognizes — yet Bram's grandmother's smuggler-songs echo in it. The Prior claims the child for interrogation. Emotional beat: a hook of recognition, the first pull toward something older than his debts.

chapters.title: Words Older than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Ordered to transcribe the child's speech, Bram realizes the language matches carvings in the deep passes — Thornfell, the erased kingdom. The child, Wren, trusts no one but begins repeating one phrase at him. Emotional beat: the scholar's thrill curdling into dread as the Prior's interest sharpens.

chapters.title: The Prior's Ambition
chapters.summary: Prior Aldous Vane's POV. Vane reveals to his inner circle that Thornfell's door holds the last dragon-fire, a power source the Concord has coveted for generations, and that Wren is the living key. Bram, listening at a vent, hears everything. Emotional beat: cold institutional hunger; the reader learns the stakes before the hero fully does.

chapters.title: A Debt Called In
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vane offers Bram freedom from his debt if he guides the Concord's soldiers through the smuggler roads to the door. Bram, terrified, agrees — then sees Wren caged like an animal and his resolve cracks. Emotional beat: the bargain that damns; complicity as a choice made in small steps.

chapters.title: The Night Road
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram steals Wren from the temple crypt and flees into the Thornfell foothills, using a smuggler's blind trail. Wren, feral, bites him and runs — then returns at dawn, drawn by Bram humming his grandmother's song. Emotional beat: fear becoming an unwilling alliance; the first fragile trust.

chapters.title: What the Ember Wants
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, fragmented and sensory. Inside Wren: the ember of the last dragon, a dying voice that shows images of a green country and a door. Wren doesn't understand being a vessel, only that the Concord's men smell like ash and ending. Emotional beat: loneliness of a child carrying something enormous.

chapters.title: The Smuggler Queen
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram seeks his old contact, Sera Voss, queen of the mountain smugglers, to buy passage. Sera agrees only when Wren's ember flares and melts her iron gate latch — proof of power worth protecting. Emotional beat: transactional loyalty tested by wonder; the found family's first recruit.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Concord riders reach the foothills; Sera's people ambush them, and Bram sees a soldier he trained with die. The rebellion is now real and bloody. Emotional beat: the cost of flight; Bram stops being a bystander to violence and becomes its participant.

chapters.title: The Heretic's Library
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with Sera. They shelter with Brother Ilex, an excommunicated archivist who has spent his life reconstructing Thornfell's erased history. Ilex confirms the door's location — the Hollow Crown pass — and warns the fire must be given freely, never taken. Emotional beat: knowledge as resistance; the erased made legible again.

chapters.title: Songs My Grandmother Lied About
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram's smuggler songs are revealed as corrupted Thornfell nursery rhymes — his family were the kingdom's last door-wardens, debt-bound and scattered after the erasure. Emotional beat: grief and fury; Bram's identity rewrites itself, and belonging has a buried address.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With Ilex teaching and the ember resonating, Wren's language surfaces into meaning: 'The door opens for the oath, not the blade.' Wren chooses Bram, pressing the ember-warm hand into his. Emotional beat: the child becomes a person with a will, not a key.

chapters.title: The Concord's Net
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane declares Bram and Wren heretics, places bounties, and turns the mountain villages against them with fear and coin. We see him justify atrocity as order. Emotional beat: the machinery of corruption grinding; power laundering itself as righteousness.

chapters.title: A Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A mountain village shelters them despite the bounty; an old woman feeds Wren Thornfell bread and weeps. But a neighbor sells them out, and the group barely escapes a Concord raid. Emotional beat: kindness and betrayal from the same soil; belonging is chosen daily.

chapters.title: The Disgraced Knight
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They rescue Serah Dane, a Concord knight who refused to burn a village, now hunted by her own order. Dane brings military knowledge and a crushing sense of failure. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected grace; the family grows by one broken limb.

chapters.title: Winter in the High Passes
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Snowbound in a cave, the group bickers, starves, and tells stories. Wren, warming the ember to keep them alive, weakens — the fire is guttering faster than Ilex predicted. Emotional beat: found family forged in shared misery; tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: The Ember's Price
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Ilex calculates the ember dies within weeks; Vane's ritual, if it seizes it at the door, will not open Thornfell but detonate its stored power, scorching the mountains. Taking the fire destroys; giving it frees. Emotional beat: the clock starts; knowledge becomes a moral burden.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Toll
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera's lieutenant sells the group's route to the Concord for a pardon. A bridge ambush scatters them; Dane is captured covering the retreat. Emotional beat: the wound of betrayal from inside the family; trust must be rebuilt, not assumed.

chapters.title: The Prisoner of Highmoor
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. In a Concord cell, Dane endures Vane's interrogation and refuses to give the pass's true name. She learns Vane's ritual requires a willing oath-bearer — and realizes Wren's trust is the weapon he lacks. Emotional beat: defiance as dignity; captivity without surrender.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain Revisited
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vane sends word: surrender Wren, and Dane lives and Bram's debt is struck. Bram nearly goes — the old hunger for freedom — until Wren says, in plain speech, 'You are my door.' Emotional beat: the temptation of self-interest against love; Bram chooses, finally and fully.

chapters.title: The Hollow Crown Road
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The remnant group — Bram, Wren, Sera, Ilex — climbs toward the door through country that begins remembering itself: Thornfell ruins warming, ghost-lights, names returning to stones. Emotional beat: awe and dread braided; the dead kingdom leaning in to watch.

chapters.title: What the Erasure Hid
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. At a wayshrine, records reveal the truth: Thornfell was not conquered but self-erased, its people sealing their power away rather than let a tyrant take it — the same choice now before Bram. Emotional beat: history as mirror; the past is an argument about the future.

chapters.title: The Rescue
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera leads a smuggler assault on the Concord's mountain garrison to free Dane, using every trick of the trade. Dane walks out carrying the garrison's own standard as a trophy. Emotional beat: competence as catharsis; the family made whole and dangerous.

chapters.title: Vane Marches
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane, furious, abandons subtlety and marches the full Concord host on the Hollow Crown, conscripting villages as he goes. He tells himself the fire will make him a shepherd of nations. Emotional beat: corruption completing itself; ambition wearing the mask of salvation.

chapters.title: The Door-Keeper's Oath
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Ilex translates the door-warden's rite: an heir of Thornfell's wardens must swear the oath and give the fire freely — and giving it may mean giving his life with it. Bram realizes the oath is his inheritance. Emotional beat: the cost crystallizes; heroism as an inheritance you can refuse.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, understanding at last what the ember is — the dragon's last heartbeat — asks it whether it wants to live or rest. The ember answers with an image of green country and open sky: it wants to be given, not kept. Emotional beat: a child's clarity shaming every adult's scheming.

chapters.title: The Concord Arrives
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vane's vanguard reaches the Hollow Crown as the group prepares the rite. Dane and Sera hold the pass mouth against impossible numbers while Bram and Wren climb to the door. Emotional beat: the last stand; courage measured in minutes bought.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Pass
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. The pass battle in full — smugglers, villagers, and one knight against the Concord host. Dane faces her former brothers-in-arms and defeats her old commander without killing him. Emotional beat: violence as tragedy, restraint as victory.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the door, Bram swears the warden's oath and offers the ember freely — but the rite demands a life, and Wren steps forward to give the child's own. Bram takes Wren's place at the threshold, the oath accepting a warden's willing heart instead. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed — not death but gift; the climax's terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire, Given
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The door opens; the dragon's fire pours through Bram into the dawn, not as a hoard but as a passing — the last dragon's power released into the land, healing blighted valleys, and gone forever from anyone's grasp. Vane arrives to seize ash. Emotional beat: transcendence and loss in one breath; the climax's turn.

chapters.title: The Prior's Ashes
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane, reaching for power that no longer exists, is consumed by the door's closing — not as punishment but as simple physics: he grasped at a fire that had already chosen. His host, leaderless, breaks. Emotional beat: corruption's end is not dramatic but empty; the void where ambition was.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram survives, changed — marked with ember-scars, half-hearing the land. Wren grieves the dragon and is held by the family. The Concord collapses into factions. Emotional beat: exhaustion and grief; the exhale after the held breath.

chapters.title: What to Do with a Kingdom's Ghost
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The victors argue: restore Thornfell's throne? Claim the mountains? Sera refuses a crown; Ilex argues for memory over restoration. The group chooses neither kingdom nor conquest but a free holding. Emotional beat: the politics of aftermath; power refused is power transformed.

chapters.title: The Debt Struck Through
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram returns to Highmoor's ruined temple and formally strikes his own debt from the ledger — then burns the whole ledger of indentures. Others follow. Emotional beat: liberation as a bureaucratic, joyful act; the chain broken at the link.

chapters.title: Wren Learns to Be a Person
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later: Wren learns letters, loses at cards to Sera, argues with Ilex about history, and plants the first garden at the pass. The ember is gone; Wren remains. Emotional beat: the quiet miracle of an ordinary childhood, hard-won.

chapters.title: Letters to the Erased
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Ilex begins the true history of Thornfell, interviewing villagers whose songs held fragments. Bram contributes his grandmother's rhymes, restored whole. Emotional beat: memory as repair; the erased given back their names.

chapters.title: The Concord's Remnant
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. Dane negotiates with surviving Concord officials, trading amnesty for the disbandment of the indenture system — using her old uniform as leverage. Some refuse; the threat isn't over, but it's smaller. Emotional beat: peace as negotiation, not miracle; vigilance without paranoia.

chapters.title: The Door That Stays Shut
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram visits the sealed door one last time. It is stone now, warm to the touch, and he tells it about the year — the way you talk at a grave. He leaves the oath-words carved fresh for whoever comes after. Emotional beat: mourning braided with gratitude; an ending acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Oath of Highmoor
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. One year on: the pass holding thrives — part village, part archive, part sanctuary. Wren, Sera, Dane, and Ilex gather as Bram takes new wardens' oaths, not to a kingdom but to each other and the road. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; the found family formalized in its own rite.

chapters.title: Green Country
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing. Wren walks the healed valleys where the dragon-fire passed, teaching other children the old words — now just a language, not a burden. The last line echoes the ember's vision: green country, open sky, a door left unlocked for the willing. Emotional beat: hope earned, not given; the future as a country anyone can enter.
